correctness.rationale: The five-dimensional lift v(x,y)=(x²,y²,x,y,1) along a first-quadrant circle arc lies in four-dimensional hyperplane. The restricted functions 1,t,t²,sqrt(1-t²) form a four-point Chebyshev family: four zeros would force a nonzero third derivative to vanish, impossible for t in (0,1). Thus every four distinct lifted rows are independent and have a unique ellipse kernel close to (1,1,0,0,-1). For finitely many sample tuples, sufficiently small perturbations preserve positive quadratic coefficients and nonempty nondegenerate conics; all five-fold determinants are nonzero on a dense-open choice because the determinant is a nonzero polynomial (an explicit five-point witness). For every selected <=4 subset, avoid the remaining finite proper hyperplanes in its valid-ellipse coefficient subspace. No five positive incidences survive; all <=4 subsets do. A dimension-5 lifted representation gives upper VC 4; along all-positive branch depth 5, each negative alternative forces next independent row, contradiction for all-positive leaf, bounding Littlestone 4. Both Sauer bounds yield exact n-polynomials. Independent rational determinant checks on seven witness points confirmed all 35 quadruple positive ellipse kernels and 21 fivefold nonincidences; the theorem for all n is analytical, not extrapolated.

final_claim: For boundaries of nondegenerate axis-parallel ellipses in R², for each n>=0 there are n distinct points such that the attainable boundary traces are exactly all subsets of size <=4; hence both static VC and online Littlestone shatter functions are sum_{j=0}^{min(4,n)} C(n,j), with VCdim=Ldim=4.
limitations: Boundary membership is equality, not ellipse interior; no rotated or filled-ellipse conclusion.
For n>=5 sample configuration requires generic perturbation; construction is existential; independent check only n=7.
